title: Street trees with diminishing shade benefit

blocks.text: A city's forestry office has `stock` young trees to plant along its streets this autumn. For each street, the arborist has measured how much summer shade benefit (in points of the city's heat index) the street gains from a number of trees, as breakpoints `xs` (trees) and `ys` (benefit), with straight lines in between. The first trees on a bare street matter most:
A street cannot take more trees than its last breakpoint (the curb runs out). Trees may be split across streets in any amounts, fractions included (the plan is rounded later).

The model in `street_trees.py` has a continuous variable `trees[name] >= 0` per street, with no upper bound, and a row keeping the total within `stock`. Write `add_benefit(model, trees, xs, ys)`: add the variables and rows you need for one street and return an expression equal to the street's benefit at the plan's number of trees. The model maximizes the sum of these expressions.
With $`S`$ the streets and $`(X_{s,k}, F_{s,k})`$ street $`s`$'s breakpoints, the model so far is
Look at the slopes of a benefit curve and at which way the objective pushes the benefit before you choose the rows. The tests use other curves of the same kind.
The tests ask for the best planting, and fix one street's trees to read its benefit, so any correct formulation passes. About six lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Street:
    name: str
    xs: tuple[float, ...]       # trees at each breakpoint, increasing, starting at 0
    ys: tuple[float, ...]       # benefit at each breakpoint


def add_benefit(model: mathopt.Model, trees: mathopt.Variable, xs: tuple[float, ...],
                ys: tuple[float, ...]):
    """Rows for one street; returns an expression equal to its benefit at `trees`."""
    benefit = model.add_variable(lb=0, name=f"benefit_{trees.name}")
    model.add_linear_constraint(trees <= xs[-1], name=f"curb_{trees.name}")
    for k in range(len(xs) - 1):
        rise = (ys[k + 1] - ys[k]) / (xs[k + 1] - xs[k])
        model.add_linear_constraint(benefit <= ys[k] + rise * (trees - xs[k]), name=f"under_{trees.name}_{k}")
    return benefit


def build(streets: list[Street], stock: float) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="street trees")
    trees = {s.name: model.add_variable(lb=0, name=f"trees_{s.name}") for s in streets}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(trees.values()) <= stock, name="stock")
    model.maximize(sum(add_benefit(model, trees[s.name], s.xs, s.ys) for s in streets))
    return model, trees


if __name__ == "__main__":
    elm = Street("Elm St", (0, 10, 25, 40), (0, 30, 51, 57))
    model, trees = build([elm], 20)
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    print(result.objective_value())

cases.says: the best planting of a small stock earns the benefit worked out by hand
a street given a fixed number of trees between two breakpoints earns exactly its curve's value there
a street given more trees than its last breakpoint is refused

origin.section: Without Binaries, the Push Must Match the Shape

concepts: a concave value that the objective pushes up, written without binaries
